hero.heading: Shopify storefronts built around the catalogue.
hero.subtitle: Theme work, product templates, and checkout-adjacent flows. Shopify stays the system of record. The storefront stops fighting it.

overview: I use Shopify when the business wants hosted commerce, inventory, and payments without operating its own stack. The work is the theme, the product story, and the pieces around checkout.
problem: A stock theme plus a dozen apps makes the product page slow and the brand look accidental. Merchandising becomes a fight with sections that were not designed for your catalogue.
solution: I shape the product, collection, and cart templates around how you actually sell, and I keep apps to the ones that earn their place.

faqs.question: Do you migrate a store onto Shopify?
faqs.answer: Yes, when the catalogue and orders have a clear source. We plan the cutover so the shop is not offline longer than it needs to be.

faqs.question: Can you build a headless storefront?
faqs.answer: Yes, with a Next.js front and Shopify as the commerce backend, when the theme is no longer enough.
